Patch release of the AnonRouter SDKs, refreshing the independently distributed
gateway trust anchor to the confidential content plane that production now
runs.

## Packages

| Package | Registry plan |
| --- | --- |
| `@anonrouter/confidential` | npm |
| `@anonrouter/client` | npm |
| `anonrouter-confidential` | GitHub wheel/sdist now; PyPI after organization approval |

The npm and PyPI jobs are separate release switches. Enabling npm does not
publish the Python package.

## Why this release is required

The `v0.1.0` gateway policy names a superseded production workload. Against the
current content plane it fails closed on the measured compose, release ID, and
platform measurements. `v0.1.1` replaces that policy with the trust anchor from
retained release manifest SHA-256
`d992b00b085d9d500d88ff926dea5c9916d29c103fe127e61273d6bde084e2a5`:

- content-plane tag `content-plane-v1.0.19`;
- image `sha256:0e7e5625538b16303c7b759e8c924f043b4da1ebfc23416f5bebaea6bb717c0f`;
- measured compose `9329f5078f9ca6fe658ec999d92a3d5d7661b7d81f60d6410ac3377ce6090f02`;
- release ID `anonrouter-tee@xl-7a84989`.

Both production hostnames were observed independently with fresh nonces. Every
pinned identity and platform field matches the retained manifest and production
policy, and each certificate key observed on the wire matches the key bound into
that hostname's quote. With the reviewed DCAP engine, both hostnames reach
`hardware_verified` with Intel TCB `UpToDate` and no failed or advisory checks.

## Install

```bash
npm install @anonrouter/confidential
npm install @anonrouter/client
```

The Python wheel and sdist remain attached to this release until PyPI
organization ownership and trusted publishing are ready.

See [`docs/release-readiness.md`](https://github.com/anonrouter/anonrouter-sdk/blob/main/docs/release-readiness.md)
for the complete gates, limitations, and artifact checks.
